title: Filipina 753 corn (Filipina corn): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Filipina 753 corn: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Filipina 753 corn is a yellow hybrid corn variety for Mindanao. About 104 days to harvest, 5.6 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: Filipina 753 corn is a yellow hybrid corn variety, also sold or known as Filipina corn or Southside Filipina 753. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2006 as NSIC 2006 Cn 178. GEMSS Gensan bred it. It takes about 104 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain, with 5.61 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Filipina corn or Southside Filipina 753, this is the same corn. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [corn variety finder](/crop-varieties/corn), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Pagtatanim ng mais, step by step](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-mais).

items: **Days to harvest:** about 104 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain.
**Yield:** 5.61 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.
**Recommended for:** Mindanao, in the dry season.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Filipina 753 corn takes about 104 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. That is about the average of the 215 yellow hybrid corn varieties with a day count, 103.6 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 5.61 t/ha trails the average of its group, 7.17. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. One tonne of shelled corn fills about 20 sacks of 50 kilograms. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 104 in NSIC trials.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took some damage but held up
Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [Corn rust](/diseases/corn-rust), [Corn stalk rot](/diseases/corn-stalk-rot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm).

The pests and diseases that hit corn fields most often: [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [banded leaf and sheath blight](/diseases/banded-leaf-and-sheath-blight), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Corn ear rot](/diseases/corn-ear-rot), [Corn planthopper](/pests/corn-planthopper). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

Its ears grew about 14.8 cm long in the trials. The shelling recovery was 77 percent, the share of the ear weight that comes off as grain. A higher share means more grain from every sack of ears. Against lodging it rated resistant, so it stood up well when wind and rain pushed the plants.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** DA 12 trials: 7.04 t/ha Sarangani lowland, 8.00 t/ha Sultan Kudarat lowland, 7.35 t/ha Sultan Kudarat highland, 5.40 t/ha Sarangani highland, 5.61 t/ha in NSIC trials, 7 to 8 t/ha in DA 12's 2025 trials.
Registry rates it resistant to lodging, corn borer and earworm.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: first among conventional yellow hybrids at DA 12's Sarangani dry season trial, and second in three other DA 12 trials in 2024 to 2025. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Filipina 753 corn

The registry recommends it for Mindanao in the dry season. Start with the color your buyer pays for: yellow corn goes to feed mills, while white and glutinous corn go to the table. Next, pick between a hybrid, which yields more but needs new seed every season, and an open pollinated variety, whose seed you can save. Then match the island group in its recommendation, because trials in Luzon and Mindanao give different winners. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for corn](/land-preparation/corn-land-preparation).

items.q: Is Filipina corn the same as Filipina 753?
items.a: Yes. Filipina corn is another name for Filipina 753, registered as NSIC 2006 Cn 178. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 104 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 5.61 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.
The registry recommends it for Mindanao in the dry season. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Filipina 753?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
